projects.name: Amazon Web Services campus, Salem Township
projects.status: Under construction. The first building is active and a second phase is under construction, with activation set for November 30, 2026; the remaining 13 of 15 buildings are due by June 30, 2029, per the campus's reported schedule.
projects.summary: Amazon's Cumulus campus beside Talen Energy's Susquehanna nuclear plant: 15 buildings on about 1,200 acres, reported at about 300,000 square feet and 48 MW per building. Talen sold the data center campus to Amazon for $650 million. FERC rejected an amended interconnection agreement for expanded co-located load, and Talen then announced a power purchase agreement with AWS that moves the existing 300 MW co-located arrangement to a front-of-the-meter framework.

figures.label: Power purchase agreement
figures.note: 840 to 1,200 MW in 2029, rising to 1,680 to 1,920 MW in 2032

projects.name: Amazon Web Services campus, Falls Township
projects.status: Under construction. Falls Township approved the project in March 2025 and the first phase has local and state approvals; a second phase needs more permits. As of August 20, 2026 the state DEP was still reviewing the permit for the backup gas generators, after receiving 1,236 public comments, and the governor's August 2026 order removed data centers from the state's fast-track permitting program.
projects.summary: The second of Amazon's two announced Pennsylvania campuses: 10 buildings and about 2 million square feet of data center space on about 250 acres of the Keystone Trade Center, a former U.S. Steel property of about 1,800 acres. The township's campus is the closest of the region's hyperscale projects to completion. PJM's market monitor asked FERC to reject the related PECO agreement in October 2025.

figures.label: Power
figures.note: No MW figure in the sources read

community.text: A petition seeking a data center moratorium in the township had nearly 5,000 signatures, and critics cite air and noise pollution and electricity and water demand. The Falls Township supervisors declared part of a separate data center zoning ordinance substantively invalid after a contentious July meeting; the article says that does not affect Amazon's project.

projects.name: Homer City Energy Campus
projects.developer: Homer City Redevelopment, with Kiewit Power Constructors; Amazon Data Services is the anticipated end user
projects.status: Announced April 2025, with power targeted for 2027. In August 2026 Amazon Data Services filed a land development plan; county planners tabled it on September 9 after more than 100 residents attended.
projects.summary: Redevelopment of the former Homer City coal station into a natural-gas-powered data center campus of more than 3,200 acres, with seven GE Vernova gas turbines. The August filing covers 36 data center buildings on about 1,100 of roughly 2,200 acres, and names AWS as the anticipated end user, though Amazon had said it had no definitive agreement.

community.text: More than 100 residents attended the September 9 county planning commission meeting, and commissioners tabled Amazon's application.

projects.name: CoreWeave data center, Lancaster
projects.developer: Chirisa Technology Parks and Machine Investment Group (tenant: CoreWeave)
projects.place: Greenfield Road and Harrisburg Pike, Lancaster County
projects.status: Announced July 2025. No later construction or approval reporting was found in this review.
projects.summary: CoreWeave said it intends to commit more than $6 billion to equip a new data center on 144 acres at 216 Greenfield Road and 1375 Harrisburg Pike, replacing the former LSC Communications and R.R. Donnelley printing plants. Co-developed by Chirisa Technology Parks and Machine Investment Group.

projects.name: Project Hazelnut (NorthPoint)
projects.status: Rejected by the township in November 2025. NorthPoint's court appeal failed, and the township adopted a six-month moratorium on data center applications that ends in January 2027. The developer is still seeking approval.
projects.summary: A proposed campus of up to 15 buildings on about 1,300 acres in the Humboldt North Industrial Park. NorthPoint has offered $10,000 to each of about 4,500 households if township leaders approve the project. Pennsylvania DEP held a public hearing in February 2026 on related stormwater permits.

figures.label: Power
figures.note: No MW figure in the sources read

community.text: One resident told the Wall Street Journal that a $10,000 payment "doesn't match how much it's going to tank my property value," as quoted by PhillyVoice.
NorthPoint offered each of about 4,500 households $10,000 (about $45 million in total) if the project is approved, and offered the township $120 million over 15 years for police and other services.
Pennsylvania DEP held a public meeting and hearing on the project's stormwater permits on February 17, 2026.

projects.name: Pennsylvania Digital I (PAX)
projects.developer: Pennsylvania Data Center Partners and PowerHouse Data Centers
projects.status: Listed as under construction by the developer, with power delivery targeted from Q4 2027.
projects.summary: Three campuses of five to six buildings each, 16 in total, on about 700 acres, with three dedicated substations. The developer lists a planned PPL switching station stepping power from 500 kV to 138 kV. Power is scheduled in stages: 450 MW in Q4 2027, 900 MW in Q2 2028, and 1,350 MW in Q2 2029.

community.text: The developer says the project will generate more than $65 million in direct tax revenue, and notes Pennsylvania's data center tax exemption, which it describes as a 100% abatement of sales and use taxes on equipment and electricity for up to 15 years. (Company claim.)

projects.name: York 2 Energy Center data center
projects.status: Planned. Announced July 2025. No approval or construction reporting was found in this review.
projects.summary: Energy Capital Partners announced plans for a $5 billion data center at the York 2 Energy Center, an existing 828 MW dual-fuel combined-cycle gas plant. The article gives no capacity for the data center itself and expects 2,500 construction jobs.

figures.label: Existing plant
figures.note: Gas plant, not data center capacity

projects.name: Air Products former headquarters site
projects.status: Abandoned. The township zoning hearing board rejected the request in July 2026, after a May 27 hearing, and Air Products said in August it would not appeal.
projects.summary: Air Products proposed three data center buildings totaling about 2.6 million square feet on its 194-acre former headquarters site, along Hamilton Boulevard and Cetronia Road. The company said no decisions have been made on the property's future.

projects.name: Project Atlas (CDE Acquisitions)
projects.status: Under township review. The zoning officer recommended denial in June 2026 on grounds of non-compliance. The outcome of the June 11 planning commission review was not found.
projects.summary: A 410-acre campus on North Cedar Crest Boulevard, across from Parkland High School. The developer cut the plan from six buildings and about 5.0 million square feet to three data center buildings, one administration building and one warehouse, totaling about 1.56 million square feet.

figures.label: Building size
figures.note: Down from 5.04M in the original plan

community.text: The township's zoning officer recommended denial of the latest plan on grounds of non-compliance.

projects.name: Project Phoenix (Aligned Data Centers)
projects.developer: Aligned Data Centers, on land owned by Frontier Group
projects.status: Construction began. Groundbreaking was reported in September 2026.
projects.summary: A three-facility campus beside the former Shippingport power station site. It will use dedicated on-site power instead of the local grid. The site previously hosted the Bruce Mansfield coal plant, and Frontier Group plans a gas plant there.

figures.label: Frontier gas plant
figures.note: Planned, with up to 3.6 GW behind the meter

projects.name: Project Laurel (MCD 7 LLC)
projects.status: Under local review. The planning commission attached 18 recommended conditions in April 2026, and the Board of Supervisors makes the final decision. No later outcome was found.
projects.summary: Eight data buildings totaling about 1.4 million square feet on roughly 192 acres across from the Philadelphia Premium Outlets, plus two administrative buildings and on-site substations. PECO has reportedly committed about 750 MW of capacity to the campus.

figures.label: PECO capacity
figures.note: Reported, not confirmed by PECO in the source

community.text: The planning commission recommended 18 conditions, including a pre-construction noise survey, updated water and sewer capacity letters, and a decommissioning bond, and said the project "should not advance without a thick layer of technical and community safeguards."

projects.name: Wildcat Ridge Data Center (Cornell Realty)
projects.status: Hearings ended September 9, 2026. Borough council said it will issue a written decision within 45 days of that hearing.
projects.summary: A campus of 14 buildings on more than 500 acres along Business Route 6 and Wildcat Road, with 588 proposed diesel backup generators. Residents have packed the hearings in opposition, raising water, power and diesel concerns.

community.text: More than 400 residents packed the second hearing in March 2026 and repeatedly shouted down testimony. Residents wore shirts reading "Stop Data Centers Protect NEPA."

An attorney for residents raised the lack of a water feasibility study. Concerns aired included water use (about 3.3 million gallons a day at summer peak), power demand (1.6 GW) and roughly 1.15 million gallons of diesel stored on site.
The proposal includes 588 diesel backup generators. The ninth and final hearing was held September 9, and borough council said it will issue a written decision within 45 days.

projects.name: Robena site (International Electric Power)
projects.status: Approved for first-phase land development in December 2025. The developer hopes to be operating by 2029.
projects.summary: A planned power plant with two turbines totaling 910 MW, meant to attract a hyperscale data center, on a 1,400-acre former mine site. A regional article called it the farthest along of the projects in southwestern Pennsylvania.

figures.label: On-site generation
figures.note: Two turbines, to serve a data center

projects.name: Archbald I data center campus (Provident Realty Advisors)
projects.developer: Archbald I LLC (linked to Provident Realty Advisors)
projects.status: Rejected locally. Archbald Borough Council voted 5-0 on March 27, 2026 to reject the conditional use application. On April 24 the developer appealed in Lackawanna County Court and published a notice claiming the application was approved automatically on March 31 because the council missed its deadline.
projects.summary: A proposed campus of up to 18 data centers on about 400 acres along Eynon Jermyn Road and Business Route 6, bordering Staback Park. The original October 2025 filing covered 22 buildings across two sites. The marker is placed at the edge of Staback Park, which the site borders; the property line is not mapped.

community.text: About 200 residents attended the March 27 special meeting, many in yellow shirts. Lackawanna County Commissioner Bill Gaughan, who has called for a statewide moratorium on new data center approvals, spoke against the project.

projects.name: Project Gravity
projects.developer: Archbald 25 Developer LLC and US Gravity Purchaser LLC (Affinius Capital)
projects.status: Under local review and litigation. The planning commission gave conditional preliminary plan approval on September 3, 2025. Valley View School District sued in September 2026 to challenge the project's exemption from the borough's data center rules. The state removed the project from the PA Permit Fast Track Program on April 27, citing the developer's unresponsiveness.
projects.summary: Seven data centers planned on a 186-acre site between Eynon Jermyn Road and Business Route 6. The plan was filed before the borough's November 2025 data center rules, which the developer argues exempts it from them. No tenant has been announced. The marker is placed at Valley View Estates, the mobile home park the campus would displace; the property line is not mapped.

community.text: Valley View School District argues the site is in none of the borough's permitted overlay districts and stresses its proximity to a campus of about 2,000 students and staff. The district's lawsuit is pending.
The campus would displace roughly three dozen residents of the Valley View Estates mobile home park.

projects.name: Project Boson
projects.status: Proposed. Filed before the borough's data center rules took effect, so it skipped the conditional use process. The reporting reviewed, through March 2026, does not describe a decision.
projects.summary: A single data center of nearly 620,000 square feet on about 83.5 acres, replacing a former auto salvage yard on Eynon Jermyn Road. It began as three buildings of about 150,000 square feet and was merged into one.

projects.name: Project Green Mountain
projects.status: Under local review. Conditional use hearings began March 19, 2026 and resume September 30 for a fourth session. After the hearings end, council has 45 days to vote and issue a written decision.
projects.summary: Seven two-story data centers up to 65 feet tall on about 271 acres of the Stavola Quarry, east of the Casey Highway. The application lists up to 28 generators and 40 roof-mounted chillers per building in a preliminary sound study.

projects.name: Newton Township data center (Popca LLC)
projects.status: Rejected locally. The township zoning officer denied the application in February 2026 because commercial uses are not allowed in the rural resource district. The developer appealed in March, then asked for a continuance of the hearing and no new date had been set.
projects.summary: Two data center buildings on nearly 76 acres on Newton Road, with two generation yards, a well, a substation and a stated cost of $280 million.

figures.label: Buildings
figures.note: 35 feet tall, 145,200 sq ft footprint each

projects.name: Dickson City data centers (Bell Mountain)
projects.developer: Dickson City Development LLC (Marzolino, per Times-Tribune)
projects.status: Under local review. Sketch plans were filed November 26, 2025. In February 2026 the borough council amended its zoning to restrict data centers to light industrial zones. No decision on the plans themselves appears in the reporting reviewed.
projects.summary: Four data centers proposed on undeveloped land above Business Route 6, behind the former Kmart. Three of them are two-story buildings with 147,000 square foot footprints under 70 feet tall.

community.text: About 300 people attended the public hearing at the Dickson City Civic Center and residents raised concerns about the proposed buildings.

projects.name: Breaker Street data centers, Jessup
projects.status: Rejected locally. The zoning hearing board unanimously rejected the developer's appeal for zoning relief on December 23, 2025, because the planned switchyard and substation sit on residentially zoned land. A written decision followed on January 2, 2026, and the developer could appeal to county court.
projects.summary: Nearly 1.1 million square feet of data centers on 131 acres south of Breaker Street, between Hill Street and the Casey Highway. Initial plans showed six 130-foot buildings drawing 600 MW.

projects.name: Blakely data center proposal
projects.status: Abandoned. The developers withdrew their rezoning application on September 12, 2025, days before a public hearing. In November 2025 the borough amended its zoning to regulate data centers.
projects.summary: Up to four two-story data centers on about 200 acres the developers asked to rezone from low density residential to commercial. The developers shifted to proposals in Dickson City.

community.text: Residents opposed the project, with widespread "No Data Center" signs and a petition gathering a couple hundred signatures.

projects.name: Scranton Materials quarry data center, Ransom Township
projects.place: 819 Newton Road, Ransom Township, Lackawanna County
projects.status: Rejected locally. Township supervisors voted 2-1 on January 20, 2026 to dismiss the company's zoning request for lack of evidence, against the solicitor's advice. The company filed a land use appeal in Lackawanna County Court in February.
projects.summary: A campus of six data center buildings on the company's 251-acre quarry at 819 Newton Road, with two stormwater ponds of about 8 million gallons each. The company filed a curative amendment in November 2025 arguing the township's ordinance unlawfully excludes data centers.

community.text: Dozens of residents and some elected officials opposed the project at several hearings, and residents handed out "No Data Centers" pins and filled out objector forms.

projects.name: I-380 data center campus, Clifton and Covington townships
projects.place: Clifton and Covington townships, Lackawanna County
projects.status: Under local review and litigation. The developer filed a substantive validity challenge to Clifton's ordinance on April 17, 2025 and a procedural challenge in county court on June 20, 2025. Covington adopted a data center district by a 3-2 vote in July 2025. The outcome of the challenges was not found in the reporting reviewed.
projects.summary: A proposed campus of up to 30 data centers on just under 1,000 acres on either side of Interstate 380, north of Clifton Beach Road. The developer cites nearby PPL 230 kV lines and fiber access.

figures.label: Buildings
figures.note: Up to three stories, about 125,000 sq ft per floor

community.text: Residents oppose the project over water and well impacts (there is no public water system), deforestation of about 1,000 acres, noise, light pollution, fire protection and power costs.

projects.name: QTS data center campus, Salem Township (Salem 2)
projects.developer: QTS Data Centers (Blackstone), land assembled by 4-3 Consulting
projects.status: Announced. The land deal closed with 96 landowners for more than $500 million, and construction is slated to begin in late 2026. The articles read do not detail a township approval.
projects.summary: A phased campus of 12 buildings on about 1,700 acres in Salem Township, using closed-loop cooling. It is the second large campus in the township, after the Amazon campus beside the Susquehanna nuclear plant.

projects.name: Salem 3 data center campus (4-3 Glennbrook Group)
projects.status: Under local review. The township planning commission voted to recommend expanding the data center overlay district to fit the project, and the board of supervisors makes the final decision. The article read, from August 22, 2026, does not report the supervisors' vote.
projects.summary: A proposed 39-building campus on more than 4,000 acres from about 200 landowners, with an on-site power plant and closed-loop water cooling. The developer says at least 80 percent of the land would stay undeveloped. The reported land deal value is $1.2 billion in one article and $1.4 billion in another.

figures.label: Site
figures.note: At least 80% to stay green space

projects.name: LBT Investment Group data center, Sugarloaf Township
projects.status: Under local review and litigation. Supervisors rejected the developer's curative amendment, the developer appealed to Luzerne County Court, and the two sides have been drafting an amendment together. On February 17, 2026 supervisors tabled it, and no data center application had been submitted.
projects.summary: LBT discussed building a data center in the township in December 2025 and filed a curative amendment arguing the zoning code did not address data centers. A lawyer for residents says LBT was not registered to do business in Pennsylvania and lacks standing, and has moved to strike the appeal.

community.text: More than 50 residents attended the February 17 meeting. Many felt the draft ordinance was shaped by the developer and said the township should write its own.

projects.name: Brewster Land Company data center challenge, Dorrance Township
projects.status: Rejected locally. The township zoning hearing board unanimously denied the company's validity challenge in May 2026, finding the ordinance does not unlawfully exclude data centers. The company's attorney said it will continue its appeal. No formal data center application has been submitted.
projects.summary: The company sought site-specific relief to build a data center on land on South Main Road in the township's highway business district. A September 2025 township amendment allows data centers only in industrial zones.

community.text: Nearly 100 residents attended the hearing at the township fire hall.

projects.name: Fit Energy data center campus, Newport Township
projects.status: Under local review. Initial zoning permits were issued in August 2026 under rules the township adopted in June 2026, which allow data centers by right in its Mixed Use District. The land sale has not closed. Residents opposed the project at an October 5 meeting.
projects.summary: A campus of 15 data centers on nearly 1,400 acres between the Glen Lyon and Lee sections of Newport Township, on land beside a quarry. Power would come from on-site natural gas fuel cells and three natural gas generation facilities.

community.text: Residents spoke against the project at an October 5 meeting, frustrated that the board had little information. A Facebook group opposing it had more than 1,200 members. The developer plans a community benefits agreement and setbacks and screening.

projects.name: Former Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill data center, Plymouth Township
projects.place: 900 Conshohocken Road, Plymouth Township, Montgomery County
projects.status: Under local review. The developer applied for a special exception to build in the township's heavy industrial district, and the zoning hearing board's procedural hearing on August 6, 2026 ended without a set date. An earlier application was withdrawn in November 2025, and the planning board had voted 4-0 against recommending it. The township council and the Montgomery County commissioners have publicly opposed the project.
projects.summary: A proposed 2-million-square-foot data center across 10 existing buildings on a 66-acre former steel mill site along the Schuylkill, with on-site natural gas turbines and closed-loop cooling according to the developer. The developer has declined to name a tenant and has also filed a validity challenge to the township's zoning.

figures.label: Developer's job estimate
figures.note: From a report the developer commissioned

community.text: Audience members repeatedly shouted down the developer's attorney and expert at the August 6 hearing. Concerns include light, noise and air pollution from on-site generation, water use, electricity costs, and proximity to homes. Gov. Josh Shapiro called the plan "the exact wrong way to do development" in a social media post.

projects.name: King of Prussia data center campus (five sites), Upper Merion
projects.place: Swedeland area, Upper Merion Township, Montgomery County
projects.status: Rejected locally. The Board of Supervisors unanimously rejected all five plans on August 13, 2026, citing a lack of specificity, including on fire safety, and failure to meet zoning requirements. On September 16 the developer filed land use appeals in Montgomery County Court asking a judge to reverse the denials.
projects.summary: A proposed 4.6 million square feet of data centers across five properties between West Conshohocken and Bridgeport, around the Renaissance business park, 411 Swedeland Road and River Road. The marker sits at the largest site (Renaissance Boulevard) and does not represent all five. Tenants have not been disclosed.

community.text: A Change.org petition had about 18,000 signatures. Residents packed township meetings and posted orange lawn signs over pollution, light, noise, electricity prices, property values and quality of life.

projects.name: Green Fig and Sentinel data center, East Whiteland
projects.developer: Green Fig Land LLC and Sentinel Data Centers
projects.place: 13 S. Bacton Hill Road, East Whiteland Township, Chester County
projects.status: Under local review. The planning commission approved the original plan in April 2024, and an amended plan with larger buildings was presented on January 28, 2026. The township solicitor said the property is zoned for data center use and that an outright denial is likely beyond the township's authority. No supervisors' vote is reported in the article read.
projects.summary: Two data center buildings of more than 1.6 million square feet on about 100 acres of a former limestone mine and lithium processing site next to a PECO substation, across from the Malvern Hunt neighborhood of about 280 homes. The amendment would make the buildings about 61 percent larger and swap cooling towers for waterless chillers.

figures.label: Site
figures.note: Former limestone mine, Superfund cleanup completed 2010

community.text: Nearly 1.5 hours of public comment, mostly opposed, raised noise, well water safety, health risks from digging at a remediated site, grid strain, utility costs and property values.

projects.name: North Coventry boutique data center proposal
projects.place: 299 W. Schuylkill Road, North Coventry Township, Chester County
projects.status: Rejected locally before a formal filing. Township supervisors voted 3-2 to reject the proposal after the developer presented it informally. The developer said it would take the project elsewhere, and supervisors asked staff to start drafting a data center ordinance.
projects.summary: A proposed "boutique" data center on an industrial lot beside Route 100, near a PECO substation and a residential development. No size was reported.

community.text: Residents strongly opposed the project and anti-data center signs appeared in yards.

projects.name: Slate Belt data center campus, Upper Mount Bethel
projects.developer: Slate Belt Holdings (Talen Energy and River Pointe owners) and RPL East LLC
projects.place: River Road, Upper Mount Bethel Township, Northampton County
projects.status: Under local review. Both companies filed zoning validity challenges asking the zoning hearing board to rule that a data center is permitted by right in the industrial zones. The hearing on the Slate Belt Holdings challenge is set for October 19, 2026. No formal development plans have been filed, and supervisors are drafting a data center ordinance.
projects.summary: A company spokesperson says both properties are part of one campus with a planned build-out of 2 gigawatts of computing power, developed in phases on both sides of River Road beside the former Portland Power plant. River Pointe sold 753 acres to Slate Belt Holdings in April 2026.

figures.label: Land sold to Slate Belt Holdings

projects.name: Lower Mount Bethel data center proposal
projects.developer: J.G. Petrucci Company and Peron Development, with Talen Energy
projects.place: Lower Mount Bethel Township, Northampton County
projects.status: Under local review. After a hearing on August 17, 2026, supervisors delayed a vote on a data center ordinance to September 14. The developers say the revised plan has a smaller footprint and does not extend onto farmland. The outcome of that vote was not found in the reporting reviewed.
projects.summary: A data center campus the developers describe as having closed-loop cooling and sound mitigation. The article does not give acreage, building count or power.

community.text: More than 250 people attended the August 17 hearing. Most speakers opposed the project, citing property values, water and electricity use and environmental impacts, and several urged an outright ban.

projects.name: South Annville data center proposal (Inch & Co.)
projects.developer: 1235 Martina Drive Owner LLC (Inch & Co. and Eastern Land & Resources)
projects.status: Abandoned. The ownership group told the township it would no longer pursue a data center, a day before supervisors were to decide on its rezoning request. A week earlier the planning commission had unanimously recommended denying the rezoning. The ABC27 page shows no exact date, and LebTown's April 8, 2026 interview with the developer is the last earlier report.
projects.summary: A planned $1.7 billion campus of five data center buildings of about 150,000 square feet each on a 99-acre site along U.S. Route 422 and Mount Pleasant Road. The request would have rezoned 13 acres from agricultural to industrial.

community.text: Residents strongly opposed the project, mainly because it would use farmland in a largely agricultural community, and held a demonstration across from the property.

projects.name: Corscale Highlands East and West data centers, Swatara Township
projects.place: Highland Street, Swatara Township, Dauphin County
projects.status: Under local review. Township commissioners approved a $120.3 million community benefits agreement by a 4-1 vote after rejecting a request to postpone, subject to the solicitor's final review of the language. Land development approvals were not described in the article read.
projects.summary: Two data center complexes: Highlands East behind the WITF building and Highlands West on the Dauphin Highlands Golf Course. The agreement pays the township in stages, starting with $7.3 million within 30 days of approval. The article gives no acreage, floor area or power figure.

figures.label: Community benefits agreement
figures.note: Paid in stages through the last certificate of occupancy

community.text: Residents asked commissioners to table the vote because the public had not seen the agreement in time to comment. One commissioner voted no, saying it lacked specific line items.

projects.name: Nebius AI campus, Highridge Industrial Park
projects.place: Highridge Industrial Park, Butler Township, Schuylkill County
projects.status: Under local review. Township supervisors voted 2-1 on about August 31, 2026 to approve an ordinance letting Nebius expand its development plan, plus a separate ordinance cutting the data center noise limit from 75 to 65 decibels. Nebius must still submit a final expansion plan for approval by the supervisors and the planning commission. Construction on the first two buildings is expected to start in late 2026.
projects.summary: A 600-acre campus beside the Walmart distribution center along Interstate 81, with a 1.2 GW supply agreement with PPL. Nebius reportedly paid $187.5 million for the property and says it can meet the new noise limit using a closed-loop cooling system.

figures.label: Power supply agreement
figures.note: With PPL; first phase 260 MW targeted for October 2027

figures.label: Site
figures.note: Reportedly $187.5M; more parcels to be bought

community.text: Residents and neighboring municipalities raised concerns about water use and noise, and about 125 people attended an early August open house. The one supervisor who voted no was Patrick Coyle.

projects.name: KRNL Data Centers proposal, New Castle Township
projects.status: Proposed. KRNL approached township supervisors about rezoning in September 2025 and no plans had been filed. No later reporting was found in this review.
projects.summary: A proposed data center on 89 wooded acres in a conservation area behind Broad Mountain Health and Rehabilitation Center, overlooking a residential street in Frackville. KRNL would need to buy the land from Mount Laurel Enterprises.

community.text: About 30 Frackville residents asked supervisors to oppose the project and presented 81 letters against it, citing light and noise, electricity and water use, quality of life and property values.

projects.name: Springdale Dynamo data center (former Cheswick plant)
projects.status: Approved locally. Springdale Borough Council granted a conditional use permit 5-2 on December 16, 2025, after approving six zoning variances. At a June 10, 2026 open house the company showed revised designs, which go to Allegheny County regulators as part of a land development permit application.
projects.summary: A data center on the site of the former Cheswick Generating Station. The June 2026 redesign moves diesel generators from the roof to enclosed ground-level positions, adds battery backup and solar, and uses closed-loop water cooling. The articles read give no megawatt, acreage or floor area figure.

community.text: About a dozen residents spoke against the project at the council vote, citing noise, pollution and appearance, and about two dozen opponents rallied outside the June open house. Some council members said they worried the borough could be sued if it rejected the proposal.

projects.name: Switch campus, Big Beaver
projects.status: Announced on April 30, 2026. The company's release gives no construction timeline or approvals.
projects.summary: A planned 382-acre campus the company says would use closed-loop water recycling with no discharge, with Switch funding the infrastructure its power needs require. No power figure was given.

projects.name: TECfusions Keystone Connect, Upper Burrell
projects.status: Under construction. TECfusions turned on the first building at the former Alcoa research site in June 2026. The company won a $2 million state grant, and its expansion plans reach 3 GW. The proposal later faced lawsuits and helped inspire a local moratorium on data center construction.
projects.summary: A conversion of the former Alcoa research and development campus, about 1,395 acres including nearby property, from 12 MW available at purchase toward a planned 3 GW. A dispute over the company's sealed pitch documents is pending in Commonwealth Court.

projects.name: Talen Energy rezoning for a data center, Montour County
projects.place: Montour County (marker at Talen's Montour power plant)
projects.status: Rejected locally. The three Montour County commissioners unanimously denied Talen's request on about February 10, 2026, saying Talen had not met its burden of proof. Talen said it still plans a data center project in the county and will refine its plans.
projects.summary: Talen asked to rezone more than 800 acres from agricultural to industrial, which would also have allowed expansion of its coal and gas-fired power plant to supply the data center. The marker is at the existing plant for reference and is not the rezoned land.

community.text: Food & Water Watch praised the denial, and local concerns included electricity bills, water use and the health effects of air pollution.

projects.name: Prologis warehouse data center, Allen Township
projects.place: 2500 Liberty Drive, Allen Township, Northampton County
projects.status: Approved locally. Allen Township supervisors unanimously approved plans in March 2026 to convert an existing warehouse into a data center. The Lehigh Valley Planning Commission was asking the developer for details on electricity use, water, cooling and emergency plans as of April 22, 2026.
projects.summary: A conversion of an existing warehouse of about 1 million square feet. No power figure was reported, and the article reports no organized public opposition.

projects.name: Quantm Group data center, 2401 W. Emaus Avenue, Allentown
projects.status: Under local review. The planning commission held a special preliminary review on July 16, 2026. Quantm pledged to withdraw its newest plans and resubmit at the commission's September 8 meeting. The project predates the city's June data center ordinance, so it is reviewed under the earlier rules.
projects.summary: An "edge data center" of almost 250,000 square feet in a vacant warehouse on Allentown's South Side, with about 66 employees. All but one of 46 truck bays would be removed to fit cooling chillers. No power figure was reported.

figures.label: Employees
figures.note: Fewer than two dozen per shift

community.text: About three dozen residents spoke, mainly about noise, water and electricity use, utility costs and effects on nearby homes. Planners flagged compatibility with Camelot for Children and the Wynnewood Greens housing complex.
